summary.summary: Charnwood ran its cash down sharply in 2025/26: treasury investments fell from £37.4m to £16.2m as capital spending — including £5.0m of unfinanced HRA works — was funded internally rather than borrowing at elevated rates, swinging the council from £14.4m net investor to £11.1m net debtor. Debt is £76.2m of legacy HRA PWLB at an average 3.38% after a scheduled £2m repayment, against a £103.5m capital financing requirement, leaving £27.3m internally borrowed. The report states plainly that borrowing long-term 'will be necessary' to fund future unfinanced capital spend and maturing debt, with a Capital Plan update due in autumn 2026 — against 1-year PWLB at 5.04% and 50-year at 6.08% at year end. It also exited both its pooled property funds (Hermes fund merger, Lothbury wind-up), crystallising just over £1m of losses which were fully provided for.

signals.headline: Treasury investments fell £21.1m in one year to £16.2m at 31 March 2026, against £76.2m debt and a £103.5m CFR
signals.why: Internal-borrowing headroom is nearly spent, so further capital spend or a cash shock pushes Charnwood into external borrowing at 5-6% PWLB rates roughly 2 points above its 3.38% portfolio average.

signals.headline: Council states new long-term borrowing 'will be necessary' for unfinanced capital expenditure and maturing debt, with financing proposals in a Capital Plan update in autumn 2026 (HRA added £4.97m unfinanced capex in 2025/26)
signals.why: A flagged pipeline of new borrowing demand arriving when PWLB rates are at their most expensive in the report's own charts.

news_drafts.headline: Charnwood expects no non-housing borrowing at year end while holding £40m of General Fund cash
news_drafts.lead:
Charnwood Council's mid-year treasury management review says its non-housing debt will be nil at the year end. The paper went to Cabinet on 12 November 2026. It says the council holds "some £40m in cash attributable to the General Fund", the account that pays for services other than council housing.

The review says the council has financed a similar amount of investment through internal borrowing. That means it has used its own cash for capital spending instead of taking out a loan.

The council's authorised limit for non-housing debt is £20m. That is the maximum total debt the council has told itself it will not exceed. The review's projected year-end position for non-housing debt is nil.
news_drafts.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Annual Investment Strategy and MRP Policy - Mid year Review

news_drafts.headline: Charnwood papers illustrate £459,520 a year in costs on £9.8m of prospective borrowing
news_drafts.lead:
Charnwood Borough Council's papers for its 2 November meeting set out £9.8m of prospective borrowing. They illustrate the yearly cost of that borrowing to the council's day-to-day budget at £459,520. The figure is made up of £276,038 in interest, illustrated at 7%, and £183,482 of minimum revenue provision (MRP), the amount a council must set aside from each year's budget to pay off past borrowing, much like a mortgage repayment.

The paper is a review of the council's capital programme, its planned spending over the next few years on things that last, such as buildings and equipment. It lists the borrowing for leisure centre repairs, Paget House Phase II, a generator, Beehive Lane and other car parks. The paper describes the borrowing as set out "together with an illustration of the ongoing revenue costs associated with that borrowing".

The paper also notes that new income from leases of the generator building and the leisure centres is expected to exceed £300k a year within three years.
news_drafts.paper_title: ANNEX Cnl 02 Nov 2026 Item XX Capital Programme Review (Cab Report)

news_drafts.headline: Charnwood repays £2m housing loan from general cash after HRA Financing Fund is used up
news_drafts.lead:
Charnwood Borough Council has repaid a £2m loan, due in October 2026, from its general cash rather than from the fund it set up for the purpose. The money was in its housing revenue account (HRA), the separate, ring-fenced account for the council's own housing stock, which is paid for by rents. The loan came from the Public Works Loan Board (PWLB), the government's lending arm for councils. The Audit Committee's first-quarter treasury management report, on how the council borrows and invests its spare cash, sets this out.

The HRA Financing Fund, the money set aside to help pay off housing debt, has run out. The report says: "A combination of investment in landlord services and rising costs have resulted in depletion of the Financing Fund and the loan was effectively refinanced via internal borrowing." Internal borrowing means using the council's own cash reserves instead of taking a new loan, which saves interest but uses up the cushion.

Housing borrowing stands at £76.19m. Once the £2m is repaid, the balance will be £74.19m. The papers give no further detail on how the general cash will be restored or what the change costs the housing account.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Annual Investment Strategy and MRP Policy - Mid year Review
findings.headline: The General Fund holds £40m of cash and has no external debt projected at year end, funded by internal borrowing.
findings.detail: The paper says the General Fund has about £40m of cash and has financed a similar amount of investment through internal borrowing. It states that non-housing debt will be nil at the year end, with the Authorised Limit for non-housing debt at £20m.
findings.matters: A General Fund with no external debt and internal borrowing covering its investment base is a structure that finance directors at other councils can compare with their own debt mix.
findings.figures: £40m General Fund cash; £20m non-housing Authorised Limit; nil non-housing debt at year end
findings.quote: The Council holds some £40m in cash attributable to the General Fund

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Annual Investment Strategy and MRP Policy - Mid year Review
findings.headline: Projections show the HRA financing fund depleting in 2025/26, a reserve previously used for capital expenditure and loan repayments.
findings.detail: The paper says the depletion leaves the HRA 'underborrowed', with existing loans below the projected borrowing requirement. It says a significant level of external borrowing will be required to maintain capital expenditure.
findings.matters: Depletion of a HRA financing reserve that funded capital and debt repayment, followed by a need for significant new external borrowing, is a position other councils with HRA self-financing will recognise.
findings.figures: 2025/26 depletion year for the HRA financing fund
findings.quote: Projections show the depletion of the HRA financing fund in 2025/26

findings.headline: A refreshed capital plan is under development, and the paper says revisions to the capital financing 'are unlikely to be immaterial'.
findings.detail: The paper says the refreshed plan may change the financing split shown in the table. It also says the capital programme is being kept under regular review due to 'ongoing budgetary pressures'.
findings.matters: A council reviewing its capital programme in response to budget pressure, with material financing changes expected, is a position lenders and peers will want to see the outcome of.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Annual Investment Strategy and MRP Policy - Mid year Review
findings.headline: The Enterprise Zone capital scheme shows £0 spent against a £5,839k budget at 30 September 2026, and the same £5,839k is shown as external borrowing.
findings.detail: The Enterprise Zone line has a full-year budget and estimate of £5,839k with no spend recorded to 30 September 2026. The financing table shows External Borrowing of £5,839k, matching this scheme's budget, while the paper says no new external borrowing has been undertaken.
findings.matters: A scheme with no spend at mid-year and borrowing tied to it is a delivery and funding timing question that other councils running enterprise zone or forward-funded schemes would recognise.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Annual Investment Strategy and MRP Policy - Mid year Review
findings.headline: Capital expenditure reached £9,547k at 30 September 2026 against a £42,582k full-year budget, and the paper keeps the budget as the year-end estimate.
findings.detail: The paper gives General Fund capital spend of £4,813k and HRA spend of £4,734k to 30 September 2026. It states that the originally budgeted figures are retained as the year-end estimate, despite challenges in completing elements of the Capital Plan.
findings.matters: Spend at roughly a fifth of the full-year budget at the half-year point, with the budget held unchanged, is a delivery position other councils can compare against their own capital profiles.

daily_post.headline: Additional borrowing anticipated in near future; timing and scale to be determined based on capital plan delivery and HRA revenue position
daily_post.lead: A lender needs visibility of borrowing outlook and timing. This signals borrowing demand exists but is not yet committed, and will depend on capital delivery acceleration and HRA cashflow.
